list.metaDescription: The evaluation methods registered on the OCI Platform. Every result names the method and version that produced it; a method version is reviewed before its results are published.
list.title: Evaluation methods
list.lead: Every result on the platform names the evaluation method and version that produced it, and a method version is reviewed before its results are published. Each method declares what it defends against, who gets to observe what, and the limits a submission must run within. The conformance specification calls these methods routes; the two words mean the same thing here.

review.heading: Review queue
review.body: {count, plural, =0 {No method version is waiting for review.} one {1 method version is waiting for review.} other {{n} method versions are waiting for review.}}

list.emptyBody: An evaluation method is registered with a threat model, a disclosure profile and an operational envelope, then reviewed. Once the first one is registered, it will appear here.

detail.metaDescription: Threat model, disclosure profile and operational envelope declared by the {slug} evaluation method, with the review status of each version.
detail.lead: {mode}. Every result on the Open Code Infrastructure (OCI) names the evaluation method and version that produced it, and a method version is reviewed before its results are published. The declarations below are what that review examines.

about.title: About this method
about.description: Who provides it, how a submission runs, and who the four parties named in the declarations are.
about.versionsNote: {count, plural, =1 {— shown below.} other {— latest first below.}}

frozen.title: Declarations are frozen once review begins
frozen.body: A version’s threat model, disclosure profile and operational envelope cannot change after it enters review, so the outcome applies to exactly what was reviewed. A change means a new version. Only an approved version produces published results; results from a version still under review are provisional, and results from a rejected or withdrawn version are withdrawn with it.

detail.noVersions: This method has no version declared yet, so it has produced no results.

threat.title: Threat model
threat.description: Who might try to learn something they should not, what this method does about each of them, what it takes for granted, and what it makes no promise about.
threat.noNote: A party marked no is named so nobody mistakes it for a guarantee: this method does not defend against it.
threat.assumptionsHint: What has to hold for the defences above to work. If an assumption fails, so does the guarantee that rests on it.
threat.outOfScopeBody: A threat model with nothing out of scope is rejected on entry; naming the boundaries is the point.

disclosure.title: Disclosure profile
disclosure.description: Who gets to see what while an evaluation runs, what that guarantee ultimately rests on, and whether a result can be reproduced.

anchorNote.CONTRACTUAL: — an operating agreement between the parties, not a technical mechanism.
anchorNote.HARDWARE_ATTESTATION: — the processor proves what code it is running before any data is released to it.
anchorNote.CRYPTOGRAPHIC: — breaking the guarantee would mean solving a problem believed to be computationally infeasible.

disclosure.notGuaranteed: Running the same submission again is not guaranteed to give the same result.
disclosure.observesHint: Everything each party can see during an evaluation, including what it already holds.

envelope.title: Operational envelope
envelope.description: The limits a submission must be designed to run within. The runtime and memory caps are enforced by the sandbox, not merely documented. Memory is given in mebibytes (MiB) and gibibytes (GiB).
envelope.measuredOn: measured on {on}. The difference between a score produced through this method and the same model scored in the clear.
envelope.notMeasuredBody: The fidelity gap is the difference between a score produced through this method and the same model scored in the clear; it is reported once measured.

declareLink.heading: Declare a new version
declareLink.body: You submitted this method. A change to its threat model, disclosure profile or operational envelope is declared as a new version, which is then reviewed.
declareLink.bodyAdmin: As an operator you can declare a version of this method. A change to its declarations is a new version, which is then reviewed.

queue.metaDescription: Evaluation-method versions waiting for a review decision.
queue.title: Versions awaiting review
queue.lead: A result counts only once the version of the method that produced it is approved. These versions are waiting for a decision. Review is in pairs: a version you submitted is listed, but another reviewer decides it.
queue.signedOutTitle: Sign in to see the review queue
queue.signedOut: The review queue is for evaluation reviewers.
queue.notReviewer: The review queue is open to evaluation reviewers and platform operators. Every method and its review status stay public on the evaluation methods page.
queue.unavailable: The evaluation methods could not be read just now. Reload the page to try again.
queue.underReviewHeading: Under review: waiting for a decision
queue.underReviewHint: The declarations are frozen. Approve or reject, with a published rationale.
queue.declaredHint: Beginning the review freezes the declarations.
queue.allEmpty: No version is waiting for review.
queue.yoursSubmitted: You submitted this method: another reviewer decides it.
queue.yoursDeclared: You declared this version: another reviewer decides it.
queue.permissionsUnknown: Open the version to see what you can do on it.
queue.count: {count, plural, one {{n} version waiting} other {{n} versions waiting}}
